title: From Brittle to Robust: Improving LLM Annotations for SE Optimization

edges.target: Senthilkumar & Menzies single-shot LLM warm-start results (negative high-dim result)
edges.ref: 54. Lohith Senthilkumar and Tim Menzies. Can large language models improve se active learning via warm-starts? arXiv:2501.00125, 2024.
edges.evidence: contrary to recent pessimistic results [54], LLMs are highly effective for optimization problems, even with high-dimensional data.

edges.target: Senthilkumar & Menzies experimental rig re-run (same MOOT data, baselines, Scott-Knott; prior tables reprinted)
edges.ref: 54. Lohith Senthilkumar and Tim Menzies. Can large language models improve se active learning via warm-starts? arXiv:2501.00125, 2024.
edges.evidence: The red results in Tables 5, 6, 7 come from prior work by Senthilkumar et al. [54] that ran the few-shot procedure of Table 4, only once (no ensembles).

edges.target: N-shot few-shot prompt template (Table 4) from Senthilkumar & Menzies
edges.ref: 54. Lohith Senthilkumar and Tim Menzies. Can large language models improve se active learning via warm-starts? arXiv:2501.00125, 2024.
edges.evidence: SynthCore is very simple to implement: it is just a wrapper around the established prompt strategy of Table 4.

edges.target: Gaussian Process Model with UCB acquisition (Brochu et al.; Williams & Rasmussen)
edges.ref: 8. Eric Brochu, Vlad M Cora, Nando De Freitas. A tutorial on bayesian optimization of expensive cost functions... arXiv:1012.2599, 2010. / 66. Williams & Rasmussen, NIPS 8, 1995.
edges.evidence: GPMs generate estimates by passing the available data through a range of kernels... a mean and standard deviation for each prediction [8, 66]. The Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) acquisition function

edges.target: Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (Bergstra et al.)
edges.ref: 5. James Bergstra, Remi Bardenet, Yoshua Bengio, Balazs Kegl. Algorithms for hyper-parameter optimization. NeurIPS 24, 2011.
edges.evidence: The Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) differs from Gaussian Process methods by separately modeling the conditional distributions p(x|y) and the marginal distribution p(y) [5].

edges.target: Explore/Exploit active learners (Lustosa & Menzies)
edges.ref: 37. Andre Lustosa and Tim Menzies. Learning from very little data: On the value of landscape analysis for predicting software project health. TOSEM 33(3), 2024.
edges.evidence: SynthCore's ensemble found optimizations that are better than state-of-the-art alternative approaches (Gaussian Process Models, Tree of Parzen Estimators, active learners in both exploration and exploitation mode).

edges.target: Active learning loop protocol (Brochu et al.; Lustosa & Menzies)
edges.ref: 8. Eric Brochu, Vlad M Cora, Nando De Freitas. arXiv:1012.2599, 2010. / 37. Andre Lustosa and Tim Menzies. TOSEM 33(3), 2024.
edges.evidence: Given n initially labeled examples, active learning proceeds as follows [8, 37].: 1. Acquire the next most informative example based on the current model. 2. Label this example

edges.target: Multi-Agent Debate (Smit et al.)
edges.ref: 56. Andries Petrus Smit et al. Are we going mad? benchmarking multi-agent debate between language models for medical q&a. NeurIPS 2023 workshop.
edges.evidence: We also explored Multi-Agent Debates (MAD) [56], but the computational costs associated with running multiple agents were prohibitive.

edges.target: Chain-of-thought prompting (Li et al.; Yang et al.)
edges.ref: 36. Jia Li et al. Structured chain-of-thought prompting for code generation. TOSEM 34(2), 2025. / 68. Guang Yang et al. Chain-of-thought in neural code generation. IEEE TSE, 2024.
edges.evidence: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting was investigated, which typically requires the LLM to generate step-by-step reasoning. However, developing an explanation module... proved to be challenging.

edges.target: Scott-Knott test (Scott & Knott; Gates & Bilbro)
edges.ref: 53. C. W. Scott and M. Knott. A cluster analysis method for grouping means in the analysis of variance. Biometrics 30(3):507-512, 1974. / 24. Gates & Bilbro, HortScience 26(8), 1991.
edges.evidence: Results were ranked using a combination of the Scott-Knott, bootstrap, and Cliff's Delta procedure [53]. Scott-Knott recursively partitions sorted treatment means... into statistically distinct, non-overlapping groups [24].

edges.target: Cliff's delta effect size
edges.ref: 11. Norman Cliff. Dominance statistics: Ordinal analyses to answer ordinal questions. Psychological Bulletin 114(3):494-509, 1993.
edges.evidence: Cliff's Delta (delta) [11] is a non-parametric effect size that quantifies the magnitude of the difference between treatment performance distributions.

edges.target: Bootstrap significance test (Efron; Efron & Tibshirani)
edges.ref: 20. Bradley Efron. Bootstrap methods: Another look at the jackknife. Annals of Statistics 7(1):1-26, 1979. / 21. Efron & Tibshirani, An Introduction to the Bootstrap, 1993.
edges.evidence: Bootstrap resampling [20] assesses the statistical significance of the observed differences... resampling with replacement from each treatment's 20 performance values.

edges.target: Cohen's small-effect rule (half a standard deviation)
edges.ref: 12. Jacob Cohen. A power primer. 2016.
edges.evidence: Cohen's rule [12] is that results are statistically distinguishable by more than a small effect if they different by half a standard deviation... then epsilon = 0.5/6.

edges.target: Geometric waiting-time model (Ross) for NEO sample-size bound
edges.ref: 52. Sheldon M Ross. Introduction to Probability Models. Academic Press, 11 edition, 2014.
edges.evidence: The waiting time to the first success can therefore be modelled as a geometric process [52]. After n draws, the probability of having observed at least one success is: 1 - (1 - epsilon)^n

edges.target: Chebyshev distance-to-ideal performance measure (as in MOEA/D)
edges.ref: 71. Qingfu Zhang and Hui Li. Moea/d: A multiobjective evolutionary algorithm based on decomposition. IEEE Trans. Evol. Comp. 11(6):712-731, 2007.
edges.evidence: To measure the effectiveness of that row, we use the Chebyshev Distance... We use Chebyshev since: It is also used by other prominent multi-objective algorithms [71]

edges.target: Low/medium/high dimensionality categorization (Di Fiore et al.)
edges.ref: 14. F. Di Fiore, M. Nardelli, L. Mainini. Active learning and bayesian optimization: A unified perspective to learn with a goal. Archives of Comp. Methods in Eng., 2024.
edges.evidence: Following a recommendation from Di Fiore et al. [14], the MOOT datasets are categorized based on their input (x) dimensionality: Low... Medium... High

edges.target: MOOT repository (Menzies & Chen)
edges.ref: 41. Tim Menzies and Tao Chen. Moot repository of multi-objective optimization tests, 2025.
edges.evidence: This study explored dozens of software engineering (SE) multi-objective optimization tasks from the MOOT repository [41] shown in Table 1

edges.target: SS-* software configuration datasets (Nair et al.)
edges.ref: 45. Vivek Nair, Tim Menzies, Jianfeng Chen. An (accidental) exploration of alternatives to evolutionary algorithms for sbse. SSBSE 2016, pp. 96-111.
edges.evidence: The Config directory consists of datasets derived from software engineering literature, specifically those labeled with "SS-*" [45].

edges.target: HPO project-health datasets (Lustosa & Menzies)
edges.ref: 37. Andre Lustosa and Tim Menzies. Learning from very little data: On the value of landscape analysis for predicting software project health. TOSEM 33(3), 2024.
edges.evidence: The HPO directory houses datasets from the hyperparameter optimization domain [37]... random forest regression models trained to forecast metrics such as commits, closed issues

edges.target: Software process model datasets: pom3, xomo, nasa93dem, coc1000 (Green/Menzies/Port et al.; POM3 after Boehm & Turner)
edges.ref: 26. Green, Menzies et al., ASE 2009 / 42. Menzies et al., ASE 2007 / 43. Menzies et al., ICSE 2009 / 49. Port, Olkov, Menzies, ASE 2008 / 6. Boehm & Turner 2004
edges.evidence: The Process directory contains datasets originating from software process modeling research [26,42,43,49]. The "pom*" datasets capture insights into agile development as studied by [6].

edges.target: Gemini 1.5 Pro (Google LLM)
edges.ref: no reference entry; named in text
edges.evidence: Hence we select Gemini 1.5 Pro, a state-of-the-art model at the time of the study, whose large context window (1M tokens)... enable it to handle the rich metadata

edges.target: Gemma-3 and Llama 3.1 (open LLMs, tried and rejected)
edges.ref: no reference entry; named in text
edges.evidence: For completeness, we also looked into other models, but Gemma-3 and Llama3.1 have two orders of magnitude fewer variables than Gemini 1.5 Pro, and they performed poorly on most of the datasets

edges.target: Fuzz4All seed-generation insight: varied few-shot examples yield diverse outputs (Xia et al.)
edges.ref: 67. Chunqiu Steven Xia, Matteo Paltenghi, Jia Le Tian, Michael Pradel, Lingming Zhang. Fuzz4all: Universal fuzzing with large language models. ICSE 2024.
edges.evidence: prior work on seed generation [67] has shown that varying few-shot examples encourages language models to produce more diverse seeds-an insight that we regard as central to our method.

edges.target: Ahmed et al. MSR'25: LLMs agree with humans on 6/10 SE labeling tasks, fail on context-intensive ones
edges.ref: 3. Toufique Ahmed, Premkumar Devanbu, Christoph Treude, Michael Pradel. Can llms replace manual annotation of software engineering artifacts? MSR'25, 2025.
edges.evidence: LLMs achieved moderate to substantial agreement with humans in 6 out of 10 tasks (e.g., non-functional requirements) [3]. However, performance declined significantly in context-intensive tasks

edges.target: NormTab: LLM difficulty reasoning over tables (Pourreza & Rafiei)
edges.ref: 50. Moein Pourreza and Davood Rafiei. NormTab: Improving symbolic reasoning in LLMs through tabular data normalization. Findings of EMNLP 2023.
edges.evidence: This experience aligns with findings from other researchers who note that tables can be particularly difficult for models primarily trained on textual sequences [50].

edges.target: Ensemble methods rationale (Dietterich)
edges.ref: 15. Thomas G Dietterich. Ensemble methods in machine learning. MCS 2000, pp. 1-15.
edges.evidence: Ensemble learning is know to boost robustness and predictive accuracy, especially in few-shot, data-scarce settings [15].

edges.target: Hou et al. SLR: only 13/229 = 5% of LLM-SE papers compare to non-LLM baselines
edges.ref: 28. Xinyi Hou et al. Large language models for software engineering: A systematic literature review. TOSEM 33(8), December 2024.
edges.evidence: a recent systematic review of 229 SE papers using LLMs found that only 13/229 = 5% compared LLMs to other approaches [28]. It is important to explore this gap

edges.target: Storm defaults 480x performance degradation vs. optimal (Jamshidi & Casale)
edges.ref: 30. P. Jamshidi and G. Casale. An uncertainty-aware approach to optimal configuration of stream processing systems. MASCOTS 2016.
edges.evidence: software is deployed with suboptimal configurations [34]. For example, Storm's defaults yield 480x performance degradation vs. optimal parameters [30].

edges.target: x264's 11 parameters need 1,536 hours to explore (Valov et al.)
edges.ref: 61. Pavel Valov, Jean-Christophe Petkovich, Jianmei Guo, Sebastian Fischmeister, Krzysztof Czarnecki. Transferring performance prediction models across different hardware platforms. ICPE 2017, pp. 39-50.
edges.evidence: Evaluating a wide range of different configurations can be very costly; e.g. x264's 11 parameters need 1, 536 hours to explore [61]

edges.target: Configuration-tuning budgets limited to dozens of evaluations (Chen et al.; Nair et al. FLASH)
edges.ref: 9. Junjie Chen, Ningxin Xu, Peiqi Chen, Hongyu Zhang. Efficient compiler autotuning via bayesian optimization. ICSE 2021. / 46. Vivek Nair, Zhe Yu, Tim Menzies, Norbert Siegmund, Sven Apel. Finding faster configurations using FLASH. IEEE TSE 46(7):794-811, 2020.
edges.evidence: x264's 11 parameters need 1, 536 hours to explore [61], limiting budgets to dozens of evaluations [9, 46]. Active learning can reduce that cost

edges.target: Valerdi: expert panels handle only 13.3 examples/hour in effort estimation
edges.ref: 60. Ricardo Valerdi. Heuristics for systems engineering cost estimation. IEEE Systems Journal 5(1):91-98, 2010.
edges.evidence: Valerdi reports studies with panels of human experts in software effort estimation. Those panels could handle only 13.3 examples/hour [60].

edges.target: Lustosa & Menzies: human ranking peaked at 15-20 judgments/hour
edges.ref: 37. Andre Lustosa and Tim Menzies. Learning from very little data: On the value of landscape analysis for predicting software project health. TOSEM 33(3), 2024.
edges.evidence: Lustosa reports studies with humans were complex management ranking peaked at only 15-20 judgments/hour [37].

edges.target: Menzies et al.: industrial SME availability rarely > 3 hours/week
edges.ref: 40. Tim Menzies, John Black, Joel Fleming, Murray Dean. An expert system for raising pigs. First Conference on Practical Applications of Prolog, 1992.
edges.evidence: In prior work with industrial subject matter experts, we found expert availability was very limited (rarely > 3 hours/week) [40].

edges.target: Yu et al. Jitterbug: 90% of false positives in technical debt analysis were labeling errors
edges.ref: 69. Zhe Yu, Fahmid Morshed Fahid, Huy Tu, Tim Menzies. Identifying self-admitted technical debts with jitterbug: A two-step approach. IEEE TSE 48(5):1676-1691, 2022.
edges.evidence: Validation Discrepancies: Manual errors are common; 90% of false positives in one technical debt analysis were labeling errors [69].

edges.target: Senthilkumar & Menzies: gpt-o1 and gemini-1.5-pro produced similar results across all dimensionality categories (justifies single-LLM design)
edges.ref: 54. Lohith Senthilkumar and Tim Menzies. Can large language models improve se active learning via warm-starts? arXiv:2501.00125, 2024.
edges.evidence: In the prior experiments from [54], both gpt-o1 and gemini-1.5-pro consistently produced similar results for all categories of the datasets (low, medium, & high dimensional).
